prompt: Standing beside a bucket of treats, Vera gave a lively fifteen-minute (speak / talk) on teaching excited puppies to sit calmly before crossing a busy pavement.
explanation_ru: После глагола give в значении «выступить с небольшим докладом или лекцией» используется существительное talk (give a talk), а не speak.

prompt: Using a colourful street map, the city planner is going to (speak / talk) us through the plan to turn two empty car park lanes into a shaded pocket park with wooden benches.
explanation_ru: Фразовый глагол talk someone through something означает «подробно объяснить кому-то план или процесс шаг за шагом»; глагол speak в этой конструкции не используется.

prompt: Holding a cold lump of butter, Priya had to (speak / talk) up over the noisy kitchen mixers during her ten-minute lesson on folding flaky pastry dough without melting the butter layers.
explanation_ru: Фразовый глагол speak up означает «говорить громче», что требуется из-за шума миксеров; talk up имеет другое значение («расхваливать»).

prompt: Standing beside a row of bicycles, the officers invited commuters to (speak / talk) out about unsafe junctions during their twenty-minute lesson on locking bikes properly and using bright reflectors on foggy winter mornings.
explanation_ru: Фразовый глагол speak out (about) означает «открыто высказываться о проблеме»; глагол talk в этом сочетании не употребляется.

prompt: Pointing a small telescope toward Jupiter, Samir gave an enthusiastic ten-minute (speak / talk) on spotting the planet's four brightest moons on a clear night.
explanation_ru: С глаголом give для обозначения короткой лекции или выступления используется существительное talk (give a talk), а не speak.

prompt: Before Liam moved into his first rented flat, Chloe offered to (speak / talk) him through resetting the fuse box and stopping a dripping tap.
explanation_ru: Фразовый глагол talk someone through something означает «подробно объяснить кому-либо, как что-то сделать»; глагол speak в этой конструкции не используется.

prompt: At the end of the dress rehearsal, Victor encouraged the actors to (speak / talk) up and project their voices toward the balcony instead of looking down at the wooden floorboards.
explanation_ru: Фразовый глагол speak up означает «говорить громче, отчётливее»; talk up имеет другое значение («расхваливать»).

prompt: Pouring steaming water over the rolled green leaves, Lin gave a calm ten-minute (speak / talk) on how water temperature changes the sweetness of mountain oolong tea.
explanation_ru: В выражении give a talk («выступить с небольшим докладом, провести беседу») используется существительное talk; слово speak существительным не является.

prompt: Olga's Czech uncle and Marco's Italian cousin can barely (speak / talk) English, yet they spend an hour happily comparing family photos and toasting with lemonade.
explanation_ru: С названиями языков (speak English) используется глагол speak, а не talk.

prompt: Petra does not (speak / talk) Spanish well, so when she asked for plasters and sun cream, the pharmacist patiently taught her two easy words and handed her a free sample.
explanation_ru: Для обозначения владения языком (speak Spanish) употребляется глагол speak.

prompt: At the castle gate, the tour guide noticed that the grandparents did not (speak / talk) English well. She switched smoothly to clear Spanish, handed them a Polish leaflet with castle maps, and later had a friendly (speak / talk) with them about the old towers. Before leaving, the grandfather spoke (to / for) the guide to thank her for her patience.
explanation_ru: С языками используется speak (speak English), в выражении have a talk нужно существительное talk, а с адресатом речи употребляется предлог to (speak to someone).

prompt: Mateo is still learning to (speak / talk) German, so he felt a little nervous in the bakery. When he tried to order boiled eggs, he accidentally (say / tell) the word for two hot hats instead. The baker laughed kindly, offered him warm bread, and had a short (speak / talk) with him to teach him the right word.
explanation_ru: С языками используется speak (speak German), перед произнесённым словом без указания слушателя нужен глагол say (said), а в сочетании have a talk — существительное talk.

prompt: During the hotel interview, the manager checked whether Nadia could (speak / talk) French and German fluently. In a quick role-play, he (say / tell) her that his suitcase was missing, and she answered smoothly. Just then, a real guest interrupted and spoke (to / at) Nadia to ask for a bucket of ice.
explanation_ru: С названиями языков используется speak, при указании слушателя без предлога — tell (told her), а при обращении к человеку — speak to.

prompt: At the museum desk, Freya asked for a Swedish audio guide, but the attendant (say / tell) her that it was out of battery. Because Freya can also (speak / talk) English clearly, the attendant happily set up an English device instead. He then spent a minute talking (about / for) the map symbols so she could find every room easily.
explanation_ru: В конструкции «сказать кому-то» используется tell (told her), с языками — speak (speak English), а для указания темы разговора — talk about.

prompt: Most of the singers in the choir do not (speak / talk) Italian, so the short chorus line was tricky for them. The director paused rehearsal to have a quick (speak / talk) with the group about pronouncing each word clearly. She joked and (say / tell) that their current version sounded like ordering pizza.
explanation_ru: С языками употребляется speak (speak Italian), в выражении have a talk — существительное talk, а перед придаточным с that без указания слушателя — say (said that).

prompt: On Yusuf's first Monday at school, Freya sits beside him with a small drawing pad. Neither of them can (speak / talk) the other's language yet, so they sketch bread, milk, and a football. As they trade easy Norwegian and Arabic words, they begin to (talk / speak) about their favorite teams with big smiles.
explanation_ru: С названиями языков и словом language используется только speak. В значении «разговаривать, беседовать» в обычной ситуации естественнее talk (хотя speak тоже возможен).

prompt: Filip can ___ English well enough to explain his solar water filter, pausing only once to check the word 'funnel' on a small paper card in his pocket.
explanation_ru: Для обозначения владения иностранным языком (speak English) всегда используется глагол speak.

prompt: Filip wants mild red pepper for his grandmother, so he tries to ___ a few Turkish words he practiced on the ferry, and the market seller grins.
explanation_ru: С указанием на конкретный язык (Turkish words) используется глагол speak, а не talk.

prompt: The Polish and Korean players do not share a fluent language, yet they smile and ___ about spin and shoes in simple English between practice sets.
explanation_ru: Для непринужденной беседы на какую-либо тему (talk about something) в разговорной речи используется глагол talk.

prompt: Marta tests a voice app to translate a Czech bakery sign, and she starts to ___ to her friend about the screen claiming the shop sells 'angry wooden slippers' instead of apple strudel.
explanation_ru: В конструкции «разговаривать с кем-то о чём-то» (talk to someone about something) используется глагол talk (say и tell здесь не подходят по управлению).

prompt: Tessa cannot read the Hungarian sign on the ticket machine, so a retired driver stops to talk English with her and explain the temporary bus route.
answer: Tessa cannot read the Hungarian sign on the ticket machine, so a retired driver stops to speak English with her and explain the temporary bus route.
accepted_answers: Tessa cannot read the Hungarian sign on the ticket machine, so a retired driver stops to speak English with her and explain the temporary bus route.
Tessa cannot read the Hungarian sign on the ticket machine, so a retired driver stops to speak English to her and explain the temporary bus route.
explanation_ru: С названиями языков используется глагол speak (speak English), а не talk.

prompt: Kenji cannot speak Italian well enough to ask for a round-trip ticket, so he uses hand gestures until the clerk prints two tickets.
answer: Kenji cannot speak Italian well enough to ask for a round-trip ticket, so he uses hand gestures until the clerk prints two tickets.
accepted_answers: Kenji cannot speak Italian well enough to ask for a round-trip ticket, so he uses hand gestures until the clerk prints two tickets.
explanation_ru: Ошибки нет: с названиями языков (speak Italian) правильно используется глагол speak.

prompt: Diego is still learning Czech, so his new classmate agrees to say slow, clear English and gives him colour-coded history notes.
answer: Diego is still learning Czech, so his new classmate agrees to speak slow, clear English and gives him colour-coded history notes.
accepted_answers: Diego is still learning Czech, so his new classmate agrees to speak slow, clear English and gives him colour-coded history notes.
explanation_ru: О владении языком или общении на каком-либо языке говорят с помощью глагола speak (speak English), а не say.

prompt: Before the forest walk starts, Amir wants to explain to the group how to tell harmless oak leaves from poison ivy. Which sentence is natural and correct?
options: Before the walk starts, Amir gives a short talk about how to recognize poison ivy along the trail.
Before the walk starts, Amir gives a short speak about how to recognize poison ivy along the trail.
Before the walk starts, Amir says a short talk about how to recognize poison ivy along the trail.
Before the walk starts, Amir talks a short speech about how to recognize poison ivy along the trail.
explanation_ru: Выступить с небольшой лекцией или инструктажем — устойчивое выражение give a short talk (здесь talk — существительное).

prompt: Rewrite the sentence using the verb speak instead of know, keeping the same meaning: Nobody at reception knows Spanish, so the night security guard translates for Carlos.
answer: Nobody at reception speaks Spanish, so the night security guard translates for Carlos.
accepted_answers: Nobody at reception speaks Spanish, so the night security guard translates for Carlos.
Nobody at reception can speak Spanish, so the night security guard translates for Carlos.
explanation_ru: Для обозначения владения иностранным языком используется глагол speak (speaks Spanish).
